body: I still haven't worked with the new config style but why is the `version` part of the `Config` when it's not configurable?
Is it really necessary to repeat all the default values from `src/configs/haskell.rs`?

I'm not too aware of `stack` and `ghc` but should you maybe check the yaml file first for a set compiler? https://docs.haskellstack.org/en/v1.0.2/yaml_configuration/#compiler Reading from file is usually faster than starting some other command

I don't think there is a need for a mutable String here. All you really want is to prepend a `v` here? You could format or simply add them. See also https://users.rust-lang.org/t/what-is-right-ways-to-concat-strings/3780
It seems that you have mixed the old config system with the new one. Check https://github.com/starship/starship/blob/master/src/modules/ruby.rs#L26-L31 about how you can write the code.

The `compiler` is optional and can't be relied on.

I'm also planning to add support for `package.yaml` and `.cabal` -styled projects, then it'll make sense to first check files for compiler version and if it isn't available - run `stack` or `ghc`.
Isnt this an unwanted additional space?
I saw that other versions does have `v`. Though, there is no space after it, so I'm removing it.
